title: Jimmie Lunceford's death
summary: He and the interviewer discuss how Lunceford died, and Stanley Dance.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: [END OF TAPE 1, SIDE B]
...die down there. Just missed killing him. It missed his heart by about that far.
Was he White or Black?

Black. Big Black stud. He was built like Lester -- and you know how Lester was built. He was built like that. I don't know what in the hell Lunceford went down for, a big, powerful mother like that. Right in front of the band! -- BOOM. Look at Bobby Plater. It's just unbelievable. Johnny Hodges, the calmest...I guess sometimes the calmest, would carry...
Yeah.
I don't know. He was on his way to the dentist, and I guess he must have been scared to death.
He was at the dentist.
He was actually probably scared to death of the dentist. Was he in the chair when this happened?
I think so, yeah.
I heard that he stepped out of the elevator and went down.
Yeah, I'm not sure now... Stanley Dance told me just how it happened, but I don't remember now.
Rowles - 48
You know, I've never met that guy. Is he here or over in Paris?
Who?
Stanley Dance.
Stanley lives in Vista, California, near San Diego. He moved out there a few years ago. It's been about maybe five years now. It's funny, you never met Stanley.
No, I never did meet that man.
Well, he was very tight with Duke. He was... Jimmie Lunceford, that was food poisoning that did it to him.
Oh really?
Yeah.
I didn't know that. I thought it was a heart attack.
It was on the road, and apparently... It must have been something really terrible that he ate, but he had an acute attack of some stomach thing, and it just killed him.
